---
title: "Hello from Quarto"
author: "Your name here"
date: today
format: html
params:
  institution: "Auburn University"
---

This is a Quarto document. The text is Markdown. The grey boxes are R code.
Click **Render** (the blue arrow above) and an HTML page opens.

## Your machine

```{r}
#| echo: false
cat("R", as.character(getRversion()), "rendered this on", format(Sys.Date(), "%B %d, %Y"))
```

## A table

The table is made by code, so it is never out of date.

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(gt)
data.frame(
  Step  = c("Write text", "Add code", "Click Render", "Hand it over"),
  Tool  = c("Markdown", "R, Python or SQL", "Quarto", "HTML, PDF, Word, slides")
) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = paste("Report for", params$institution))
```

## A chart

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 3
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point(colour = "#0C2340") +
  labs(x = "Weight", y = "Miles per gallon", title = "Any chart you can make in R goes here") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Try one thing

1. Change `author` at the top to your name and Render again.
2. Change `format: html` to `format: typst` and Render. You get a PDF.
3. Change it to `format: docx`. You get Word.
